title: Chapter 4 Quiz 9
description: Keeping data after the program ends.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Why do we need **files**?
options: Files keep data after the program ends
Files are smaller than arrays in memory
Files make the program run faster
Files replace the need for variables
questions.explanation: Arrays, records and variables live only as long as the program. Watch out: RAM is volatile, so its content is lost.

questions.question: Which are non-volatile media?
options: RAM memory
A magnetic tape
A CPU register
A USB key
A hard disk
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; the others keep data. Watch out: RAM is fast, but it forgets everything when the power goes off.

questions.question: What is a **file** in the course?
options: A single variable stored on disk
A set of loops stored with a name
An index kept inside the memory of RAM
A set of records with a name on a medium
questions.explanation: A file groups records describing the same entity.

questions.question: What is a **record** of a file?
options: The values of one entity's attributes
A loop that reads the whole file
The name of the file on the disk
The medium where the file is stored
questions.explanation: A record completely defines one entity: one student, one product…

questions.question: Put the steps in order for writing a line to a file and reading it back.
questions.explanation: Write mode, write, close, read mode, read, close.

questions.question: Match each Pascal instruction to what it does.
right: Links the file variable to a file name
Tells whether the end of the file is reached
questions.explanation: These are the instructions of the course example.

questions.question: What does rewrite(MyFile) do if the file already exists?
options: It opens the file for reading
It overwrites the old content
It adds text to the end
It refuses to open the file
questions.explanation: rewrite creates the file if it does not exist, otherwise overwrites it. Watch out: it does not append, the old content is lost.

questions.question: Complete the reading loop.
questions.code:
reset(MyFile)
while {{1}} eof(MyFile) do
    readln(MyFile, TextToRead)
    writeln('File content: ', TextToRead)
EndDo
{{2}}(MyFile)
questions.explanation: We loop while the end is not reached, then close the file.

questions.question: This should read back a text that was written to the file. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
options: reset(MyFile)
eof(MyFile)
close(MyFile)
assign(MyFile)
questions.explanation: To read a file we open it with reset. Watch out: rewrite opens for writing and erases the old content.
